method.label: Convert the repeating tail to a fraction

annotationRationale: The derivation converts the repeating block to a fraction by shifting and subtracting, then models the product error with a linear equation.
sourceMethod: Followed the official repeating-tail difference method, supplying the shift-and-subtract derivation of the block's fraction n/99.

review.mathCheck: Writing \(n=\overline{ab}\) gives \(66(n/99-n/100)=n/150=1/2\), so \(n=75\), choice E. The products are indeed 116 and 115.5.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 5: isolate the repeating tail and convert it using denominator 99. The added shift-and-subtract derivation explains the conversion fully.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed conversion and linear modeling concepts fit; equality transformations appropriately serve as background.
